question: A stone dropped down a well falls 4.9 m in its first second. How many metres has it fallen after 3 seconds?
move: When something keeps speeding up, expect totals to outrun the time spent.
ask: What in my life is gathering speed, so that waiting twice as long means far more than twice the result?
trap: Tripling 4.9 m to about 15 m, as if speed stayed fixed.
hint: Ask whether distance grows with the time, or with the time multiplied by itself.
steps: Distance fallen grows with time squared: 4.9 m × t².
reference: Galileo, Dialogues Concerning Two New Sciences, trans. Crew & de Salvio, Macmillan, 1914
